newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, ignores GCA stock data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, ignores GCA stock data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures posted losses for the third consecutive session Wednesday, battered by a steady dose of commission house and speculative selling, traders said.
Benchmark December futures fell 2.00 cents per lb on the day, to 112.20, having traded from 116.25 to 111.75. Second-month March lost 1.65, to settle at 103.55.

Today's downturn came despite a substantial drawdown in U.S. consumer stocks last month. The Green Coffee Associaton of New York reported Tuesday that supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses declined in September by 205,000 60-kg bags, to 1,611,000 bags.
Most traders had expected GCA stocks to fall by 100,000 to 200,000 bags.
"Everyone knows there is a tight supply of coffee," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "But this market has come up so much (that) a bit of a correction is to be expected.
"The point is, if we had not trended higher the last two weeks, it may have responded to the GCA data," Ganes added."

Nearby supply jitters carried the spot December contract to a six-week high of 116.30 cents on Friday -- up some 13 percent since the start of October -- and pushed out the December/March switch to a hefty 9.00 cents.
The nearby switch eased slightly Wednesday, ending at 8.65 cents compared to 9.00 cents at the close Tuesday.

Dealers said the GCA figures did prompt a round of trade buying at the open, which carried the market to its intraday highs. But origin selling above 115.00 cents basis December quickly stemmed the gains and turned the momentum to the downside.
Keen roaster interest was noted below the 112.50 level, but a late bout of local selling kept prices down, dealers said.

Technically, traders said the December contract's ability to hold support at 111.50 cents today could be viewed as constructive. They put December's next downside target at 110.25. To the upside, strong resistance was noted at 118.50.

On the fundamental side, traders continued to keep an eye on the trucker strike in Colombia, which entered its third day Wednesday. Exporters said the work stoppage has halted all shipments of coffee to Colombian ports.
The day's turnover was relatively heavy, at an estimated 9,863 lots.
